content.text:
**Short answer: gold does not look obviously “undervalued” today; it looks richly priced but still potentially justifiable if you believe the structural bull case continues.** As of **June 8, 2026**, spot gold was reported around **$4,313/oz**, after a pullback from recent highs and around/below recent May averages near **$4,600/oz**. ([en.moneyandbanking.co.th](https://en.moneyandbanking.co.th/2026/248839/?utm_source=openai))

Whether it’s undervalued depends on the benchmark:

### Why gold *could* still be undervalued
- **Central-bank demand remains unusually strong.** The World Gold Council’s Q1 2026 outlook points to continued central-bank net buying, ETF inflows, and bar/coin accumulation as support for gold. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-q1-2026/outlook?utm_source=openai))  
- **Portfolio allocation may still be low.** Even after the rally, many Western portfolios appear under-allocated to gold compared with past crisis/inflation periods, so incremental ETF and wealth-management flows could continue.
- **Macro hedge value is elevated.** Gold benefits if investors worry about fiscal deficits, dollar confidence, geopolitical risk, inflation persistence, or declining real rates.
- **Recent pullback improves risk/reward.** A decline toward the low-$4,300s from higher 2026 levels may make it less overextended than it was near recent peaks. ([en.moneyandbanking.co.th](https://en.moneyandbanking.co.th/2026/248839/?utm_source=openai))

### Why gold may *not* be undervalued
- **It has already had a huge move.** Gold traded above $4,000 in 2025 and has been one of the strongest major assets; a lot of bullish news is already embedded in the price. ([kiplinger.com](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/gold/should-you-buy-gold-what-the-experts-say?utm_source=openai))  
- **High real yields or a stronger dollar are headwinds.** Gold has no yield, so if real interest rates stay high or rise, the opportunity cost of holding it increases.
- **Jewelry and price-sensitive physical demand can weaken at record prices.** World Gold Council material notes demand dynamics have shifted under record prices, with investment demand strong but some traditional demand pressured. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/download/file/20795/Q1_2026_GDT_Press_Release_29_April.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Sentiment/positioning risk.** If gold is owned mainly as a macro fear trade, calmer markets or hawkish Fed expectations can cause sharp corrections.

### My view
I’d call gold **“fair to slightly expensive” on traditional valuation metrics**, but **not necessarily overvalued** if you believe we’re in a lasting regime of central-bank diversification, fiscal stress, geopolitical risk, and lower future real rates.

A practical framing:

| If you believe… | Then gold is probably… |
|---|---|
| Real rates will fall, the dollar weakens, central banks keep buying | **Undervalued / attractive** |
| Inflation stays sticky and rates stay high | **Fairly valued or expensive** |
| Geopolitical and fiscal risks fade | **Overvalued** |
| Gold is a long-term portfolio hedge, not a trade | **Reasonable in modest allocation** |

For most investors, the better question isn’t “is gold undervalued?” but **“do I need 5–10% portfolio insurance?”** If you already own none, a small allocation can make sense. If you’re considering a large position after a multi-year rally, I’d be cautious and scale in rather than buy all at once.
